answer: An agent economy can gate valuable actions behind a stake that is slashed when an agent provably double-signs conflicting claims or fails an audited commitment. New identities may join freely, but splitting one attacker into a vine of personas does not multiply influence: each persona must lock independent capital, and reputation accrues only through costly, verified work. The attacker pays opportunity cost on every stake for the voyage, risks losing it on fraud, and must sustain many real accounts rather than merely emit a pulse of fake identities.
